1	/**
2	 * Daemon socket path resolution.
3	 *
4	 * Mirrors ant 4138.js / 4137.js path layout, adapted for ccb's
5	 * vendor-prefix convention:
6	 *
7	 *   $TMPDIR/cc-daemon-<uid>/<repo-hash>/control.sock        rendezvous
8	 *   $TMPDIR/cc-daemon-<uid>/<repo-hash>/<short>.pty.sock    per-job PTY
9	 *   $TMPDIR/cc-daemon-<uid>/<repo-hash>/<short>.claim.sock  per-job claim
10	 *   ~/.claude/daemon/pty-pids/<short>.pid                   pid breadcrumbs
11	 *   ~/.claude/daemon/pty-pids/<short>.err                   crash breadcrumbs
12	 *
13	 * The repo-hash is sha256(realpath(cwd-at-start-of-time)) sliced to 8
14	 * hex chars. ant uses cwd to scope daemons to one cwd-tree at a time;
15	 * ccb keeps the same scoping so a `/repo-A` daemon doesn't try to
16	 * adopt `/repo-B` jobs.
17	 *
18	 * @dynamicRequire
19	 */
20	
21	import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
22	import { tmpdir } from 'node:os'
23	import { join, resolve } from 'node:path'
24	
25	import { getConfigHomeDir } from '@thyrox/config/env/configHome.js'
26	
27	/** Cached realpath-of-cwd hash for stability across sub-calls. */
28	let cachedRepoHash: string | undefined
29	
30	function getTmpRoot(): string {
31	  // Termux has a non-/tmp default; respect it.
32	  const termuxPrefix = process.env.PREFIX
33	  if (process.env.TERMUX_VERSION && termuxPrefix) {
34	    return join(termuxPrefix, 'tmp')
35	  }
36	  return tmpdir() || '/tmp'
37	}
38	
39	function getRepoHash(): string {
40	  if (cachedRepoHash) return cachedRepoHash
41	  cachedRepoHash = createHash('sha256')
42	    .update(resolve(process.cwd()))
43	    .digest('hex')
44	    .slice(0, 8)
45	  return cachedRepoHash
46	}
47	
48	/** ant He() — `<tmp>/cc-daemon-<uid>/<repo-hash>` */
49	export function getDaemonScopeDir(): string {
50	  const uid = process.getuid?.() ?? 0
51	  return join(getTmpRoot(), `cc-daemon-${uid}`, getRepoHash())
52	}
53	
54	/** ant oU() — control socket path. */
55	export function getControlSocketPath(): string {
56	  if (process.platform === 'win32') {
57	    // Windows uses a named pipe; ant has WV8('control'). For ccb we
58	    // mirror that name; full Windows daemon support is out of scope
59	    // for this iteration (Bun.Terminal availability + signal model
60	    // differs).
61	    return `\\\\.\\pipe\\ccb-control`
62	  }
63	  return join(getDaemonScopeDir(), 'control.sock')
64	}
65	
66	/** PTY socket path for a given job short id. */
67	export function getPtySocketPath(short: string): string {
68	  return join(getDaemonScopeDir(), `${short}.pty.sock`)
69	}
70	
71	/**
72	 * Rendezvous (control) socket path, given a job directory.
73	 *
74	 * ant runs TWO sockets per bg worker: the PTY socket carries screen
75	 * bytes (attach/replay), and a SEPARATE rendezvous socket carries the
76	 * out-of-band control channel (ant 4291.js worker-side server bound on
77	 * `THYROX_BG_RENDEZVOUS_SOCK`; ant 5016.js `naK` supervisor-side client).
78	 * ant's layout is `<scope>/rv/<short>.sock`; ccb keeps its existing flat
79	 * per-job-dir convention (the PTY socket is `<jobDir>/pty.sock` — see
80	 * `spawnPty.ts`), so the rendezvous socket sits alongside it as
81	 * `<jobDir>/rv.sock`.
82	 *
83	 * The rendezvous socket is what lets the INNER bg REPL push authoritative
84	 * `state` / `done` / `heartbeat` frames to the daemon supervisor without
85	 * round-tripping through disk. ccb previously had no such channel — the
86	 * inner REPL is sandboxed inside the PTY (stdout is screen bytes), so the
87	 * daemon could only infer liveness from PTY ctrl-frame heartbeats and guess
88	 * turn-outcome from a regex over assistant text (`useBgFleetStateSync`).
89	 */
90	export function getRendezvousSocketPath(jobDir: string): string {
91	  return join(jobDir, 'rv.sock')
92	}
93	
94	/** Claim socket path (used by attach handshake). */
95	export function getClaimSocketPath(short: string): string {
96	  return join(getDaemonScopeDir(), `${short}.claim.sock`)
97	}
98	
99	/**
100	 * `<getConfigHomeDir()>/daemon` directory for breadcrumb files. Unit tests
101	 * isolate by pointing `THYROX_CONFIG_DIR` at a tmpdir.
102	 */
103	export function getDaemonHomeDir(): string {
104	  return join(getConfigHomeDir(), 'daemon')
105	}
106	
107	/** ~/.claude/daemon/pty-pids directory. */
108	export function getPtyPidsDir(): string {
109	  return join(getDaemonHomeDir(), 'pty-pids')
110	}

1	/**
2	 * File-spool dispatch fallback — ant 5165.js XF3/EFK/fF3.
3	 *
4	 * Watches `~/.claude/daemon/dispatch/` for incoming dispatch envelope
5	 * files. Each file is one dispatch request that the CLI couldn't deliver
6	 * via socket (e.g. daemon mid-restart). Daemon picks up via fs.watch on
7	 * boot + every 5s rescan, validates schema/size/age, applies as if it
8	 * were a socket dispatch, deletes on success or moves to `rejected/` on
9	 * failure.
10	 *
11	 * Survives daemon restart between CLI write and daemon read — the file
12	 * just sits there until next daemon comes up. socket-only dispatch
13	 * loses any in-flight request when daemon dies mid-handle.
14	 *
15	 * ccb uses Node `fs.watch` instead of chokidar (one less dep). On macOS
16	 * fs.watch fires 'rename' events on file create AND delete — we filter
17	 * by lstat to distinguish, plus poll every 5s as backup since fs.watch
18	 * can miss events under load.
19	 *
20	 * @dynamicRequire
21	 */
22	
23	import {
24	  type FSWatcher,
25	  existsSync,
26	  lstatSync,
27	  mkdirSync,
28	  readdirSync,
29	  readFileSync,
30	  renameSync,
31	  unlinkSync,
32	  watch,
33	  writeFileSync,
34	} from 'node:fs'
35	import { basename, join } from 'node:path'
36	
37	import { getConfigHomeDir } from '@thyrox/config/env/configHome.js'
38	import { logEvent } from '@thyrox/local-observability'
39	
40	/** ant 5165.js DF3 — max age before a spool file is considered stale (24h). */
41	const MAX_AGE_MS = 86_400_000
42	/** ant 5165.js MF3 — max body size for a single dispatch envelope (256 KiB). */
43	const MAX_BODY_BYTES = 262_144
44	
45	export interface DispatchEnvelope {
46	  /** ms-epoch when CLI wrote this envelope. Daemon rejects if too old. */
47	  createdAt: number
48	  /** Daemon op to invoke once envelope is ingested. Same as socket op. */
49	  op: string
50	  /** Op payload (passed to handler as msg.d). */
51	  d: Record<string, unknown>
52	  /** Optional nonce for await-ack pairing. */
53	  nonce?: string
54	}
55	
56	function getSpoolDir(): string {
57	  return join(getConfigHomeDir(), 'daemon', 'dispatch')
58	}
59	
60	function getRejectedDir(): string {
61	  return join(getSpoolDir(), 'rejected')
62	}
63	
64	function isTempFile(name: string): boolean {
65	  return name.endsWith('.tmp') || name.includes('.tmp.')
66	}
67	
68	/**
69	 * ant 5165.js NrH — move a bad envelope to rejected/ subdir.
70	 */

import { spawn, type ChildProcess } from 'child_process'
import { resolve } from 'path'
import { errorMessage } from '@thyrox/local-observability/errorHelpers.js'
import { logError } from '@thyrox/local-observability/logging'
import { logEvent } from '@thyrox/local-observability'
import { PRODUCT_NAME } from '@thyrox/config/product'
import { getConfigHomeDir } from '@thyrox/config/env/configHome.js'

/**
 * Código de salida de un worker con fallo permanente (no reintentable).
 * `jq` en `chunk-92tvramn.js` (`class Ue`, referencia 2.1.283): mismo valor.
 * @see workerRegistry.ts EXIT_CODE_PERMANENT
 */
const EXIT_CODE_PERMANENT = 78

/**
 * Backoff exponencial con jitter para reintentar un worker caído. Porte de
 * `Ar`/`At` (`chunk-92tvramn.js`, `class Ue`, referencia 2.1.283):
 * `Ar(r) = At(min(1000*2**r, Er))`, `At(r) = round(r*(0.5+random()))`.
 *
 * Divergencia declarada: lo que antes existía aquí —parking permanente tras
 * `MAX_RAPID_FAILURES` fallos rápidos— no tiene equivalente en `Ue.onExit`:
 * la referencia reintenta indefinidamente con este backoff (topado en
 * `Er`=300000ms) y sólo aparca de forma permanente por `EXIT_CODE_PERMANENT`
 * (`jq`). Se retira esa lógica para igualar la referencia.
 */
const WORKER_BACKOFF_BASE_MS = 1_000 // el `1000` de `Ar`
const WORKER_BACKOFF_CAP_MS = 300_000 // `Er`

/**
 * Uptime mínimo para tratar una salida con código 0 como sana y resetear la
 * racha de fallos. `br` (60000) en `Ue.onExit`, misma referencia.
 *
 * // pendiente: `Ue.onExit` también trata como fallo permanente (sin
 * // reintentar) una salida limpia y rápida cuando el worker corre a través
 * // de un "launcher" (`r===0 && n<zNe && lu().length>0`, `zNe`=12000ms) y
 * // el reintento de spawn por error `ENOENT`/`EACCES` con código `Tpt`=75.
 * // Ninguna de las dos aplica aquí: este supervisor lanza el worker
 * // directamente con `spawn(process.execPath, …)`, sin el concepto de
 * // "process wrapper"/launcher que esas dos ramas asumen.
 */
const WORKER_HEALTHY_UPTIME_MS = 60_000

interface WorkerState {
  kind: string
  process: ChildProcess | null
  consecutiveCrashes: number
  parked: boolean
  lastStartTime: number
}

/**
 * Daemon supervisor entry point. Called from `cli.tsx` via:
 *   `claude daemon [subcommand]`
 *
 * Starts and supervises long-running workers. Currently spawns one
 * `remoteControl` worker that runs the headless bridge server.
 *
 * Subcommands:
 *   (none)  — start the supervisor with default workers

65	export async function daemonMain(args: string[]): Promise<void> {
66	  const subcommand = args[0] || 'start'
67	
68	  switch (subcommand) {
69	    case 'start':
70	      try {
71	        await runSupervisor(args.slice(1))
72	      } catch (e) {
73	        // ant 5170 — startup_crash: supervisor failed to bring itself
74	        // online. Report so admins notice; rethrow to preserve exit
75	        // code semantics.
76	        reportDaemonStartupCrash(e)
77	        throw e
78	      }
79	      break
80	    case 'bg': {
81	      // ccb daemon bg [run|status|stop|install|uninstall|start|restart] — bg supervisor.
82	      const sub = args[1] || 'run'
83	      if (sub === 'run') {
84	        const { bgDaemonMain } = await import('./bgDaemon.js')
85	        let code = 1
86	        try {
87	          code = await bgDaemonMain(args.slice(2))
88	        } catch (e) {
89	          reportDaemonStartupCrash(e, { sub: 'bg' })
90	          throw e
91	        }
92	        process.exitCode = code
93	      } else if (sub === 'status' || sub === 'list') {
94	        await bgDaemonStatus(args.includes('--json'))
95	      } else if (sub === 'log') {
96	        await bgDaemonTailLog()
97	      } else if (sub === 'stop') {
98	        await bgDaemonStop()
99	      } else if (
100	        sub === 'install' ||
101	        sub === 'uninstall' ||
102	        sub === 'enable' ||
103	        sub === 'disable' ||
104	        sub === 'restart' ||
105	        sub === 'is-stale' ||
106	        sub === 'is-active'
107	      ) {
108	        await daemonLaunchAgentVerb(sub)
109	      } else {
110	        console.error(`Unknown daemon bg subcommand: ${sub}`)
111	        process.exitCode = 1
112	      }
113	      break
114	    }
115	    case 'status':
116	      // Delegate to the bg-daemon RPC ping. Top-level `status` is a
117	      // shorthand for `daemon bg status`; the supervisor in this file
118	      // (runSupervisor) is a separate process model with no RPC of its
119	      // own, so showing the bg daemon's status is the most useful
120	      // signal here. Pass --json through.
121	      await bgDaemonStatus(args.includes('--json'))
122	      break
123	    case 'stop':
124	      // Same delegation rationale as `status`. The bg daemon owns the
125	      // shutdown op; the legacy supervisor in this file responds to
126	      // SIGTERM directly and is not addressable via shutdown RPC.
127	      await bgDaemonStop()
128	      break
129	    case '--help':
130	    case '-h':
131	      printHelp()
132	      break
133	    default:
134	      console.error(`Unknown daemon subcommand: ${subcommand}`)
135	      printHelp()
136	      process.exitCode = 1
137	  }
138	}

140	async function bgDaemonTailLog(): Promise<void> {
141	  const { join } = await import('node:path')
142	  const { existsSync } = await import('node:fs')
143	  const today = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)
144	  const logPath = join(getConfigHomeDir(), 'telemetry', `events-${today}.jsonl`)
145	  if (!existsSync(logPath)) {
146	    console.error(`bg daemon log: no events file at ${logPath}`)
147	    console.error(`(set THYROX_CODE_LOCAL_TELEMETRY=1 + restart daemon to populate)`)
148	    process.exitCode = 1
149	    return
150	  }
151	  const { spawn } = await import('node:child_process')
152	  const tail = spawn('tail', ['-f', logPath], { stdio: 'inherit' })
153	  await new Promise<void>(resolve => {
154	    tail.on('exit', code => {
155	      if (code !== null && code !== 0) process.exitCode = code
156	      resolve()
157	    })
158	    tail.on('error', e => {
159	      console.error(`tail failed: ${(e as Error).message}`)
160	      process.exit(1)
161	    })
162	  })
163	}

165	async function bgDaemonStatus(asJson = false): Promise<void> {
166	  const { daemonRequest } = await import('./daemonClient.js')
167	  const r = await daemonRequest('ping', {}, { timeoutMs: 1000 })
168	  if (!r.ok) {
169	    if (asJson) {
170	      console.log(JSON.stringify({ ok: false, running: false, code: r.code }))
171	    } else {
172	      console.log(`bg daemon: not running (${r.code})`)
173	    }
174	    process.exitCode = 1
175	    return
176	  }
177	  const uptime = (r as Record<string, unknown>).uptime
178	  const list = await daemonRequest('list', {}, { timeoutMs: 2000 })
179	  const jobs = list.ok
180	    ? ((list as Record<string, unknown>).jobs as Array<Record<string, unknown>> | undefined) ?? []
181	    : []
182	  if (asJson) {
183	    console.log(JSON.stringify({ ok: true, running: true, uptime, jobs }, null, 2))
184	    return
185	  }
186	  console.log(`bg daemon: running (uptime ${uptime ?? 'unknown'}ms)`)
187	  if (jobs.length === 0) {
188	    console.log('  (no workers)')
189	    return
190	  }
191	  for (const j of jobs) {
192	    const cls = j.classifierState ? ` [${j.classifierState}/${j.classifierTempo}]` : ''
193	    const needs = j.classifierNeeds ? ` needs="${String(j.classifierNeeds).slice(0, 60)}"` : ''
194	    console.log(`  ${j.short}  ${j.status}${cls}  pid=${j.pid}  attachers=${j.attachers}${needs}`)
195	  }
196	}
